hints: Use polynomial long division, matching the leading term $x^4$ first with a multiple of $x^2+2x-1$.
After each subtraction, repeat with the new leading term until the remainder has degree less than $2$.
walkthrough: Set up polynomial long division of the dividend $x^4 + 0x^3 + 0x^2 + 0x + 0$ by the divisor $x^2 + 2x - 1$.

Divide the leading term $x^4$ by $x^2$ to obtain the first term of the quotient:
$$\dfrac{x^4}{x^2} = x^2$$

Multiply the divisor $x^2 + 2x - 1$ by $x^2$ and subtract from the dividend:
$$x^2(x^2 + 2x - 1) = x^4 + 2x^3 - x^2$$
$$(x^4) - (x^4 + 2x^3 - x^2) = -2x^3 + x^2$$

Divide the new leading term $-2x^3$ by $x^2$ to obtain the second term of the quotient:
$$\dfrac{-2x^3}{x^2} = -2x$$

Multiply the divisor by $-2x$ and subtract:
$$-2x(x^2 + 2x - 1) = -2x^3 - 4x^2 + 2x$$
$$(-2x^3 + x^2) - (-2x^3 - 4x^2 + 2x) = 5x^2 - 2x$$

Divide the leading term $5x^2$ by $x^2$ to obtain the third term of the quotient:
$$\dfrac{5x^2}{x^2} = 5$$

Multiply the divisor by $5$ and subtract to find the remainder:
$$5(x^2 + 2x - 1) = 5x^2 + 10x - 5$$
$$(5x^2 - 2x) - (5x^2 + 10x - 5) = -12x + 5$$

State the quotient and remainder:
$$\text{Quotient} = x^2 - 2x + 5, \quad \text{Remainder} = -12x + 5$$
